query: Why do some travel expenses get declined, and which factors contribute the most?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: The type of asset/expense being submitted plausibly affects decline likelihood and is a candidate cause of the outcome; it is a categorical driver rather than a common cause of another treatment.

per_column.name: procurement_urgency
per_column.rationale: Urgency of procurement could plausibly drive whether an expense is declined; treated as a candidate cause of the outcome.

per_column.name: expense_categorization_clarity
per_column.rationale: Whether the expense purpose is clear/ambiguous plausibly causes declines directly; it is a candidate driver rather than a common cause of a separate treatment.

per_column.name: travel_intent_explicit
per_column.rationale: Whether travel intent is explicit is closely tied to the travel-expense framing of the query. It is a candidate cause of declines but is essentially named/implied by the query focus on travel expenses.

per_column.name: processing_lag
per_column.rationale: Processing lag is more plausibly a downstream consequence of the submission/decision process rather than a common cause of both a treatment and the outcome; conditioning on it risks bias.

per_column.name: department_expense_pattern
per_column.rationale: Department plausibly influences both the kind/urgency of expenses submitted (treatments) and the decline rate (differing budgets/policies), making it a genuine common cause that must be adjusted for.

per_column.name: asset_value_tier
per_column.rationale: Expense value tier plausibly affects both what category/urgency of item is submitted and the scrutiny/decline likelihood, acting as a common cause.

per_column.name: user_submission_frequency
per_column.rationale: A user's submission frequency plausibly influences both the types/quality of expenses submitted (treatments) and their decline outcome (habitual vs error-prone submitters), a common cause not stated in the query.

judge.rationale: The added columns supply candidate treatments (asset category, urgency, categorization clarity, travel intent) and several plausible common causes of both treatment and outcome (department, asset value tier, user submission frequency), all surfaced from data rather than named in the query. This constitutes real causal-attribution structure. Quality is moderate rather than high: one column (processing_lag) is better understood as a downstream collider/consequence and should not be adjusted for, and the confounders, while genuine common causes, are somewhat generic and their confounding role over the specified treatments is only moderately strong.
